bib.title: Shepherd: A Critic for Language Model Generation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Shepherd: A Critic for Language Model Generation", Tianlu Wang, Ping Yu, Xiaoqing Ellen Tan, Sean O'Brien, Ramakanth Pasunuru, Jane Dwivedi-Yu, Olga Golovneva, Luke Zettlemoyer, Maryam Fazel-Zarandi, Asli Celikyilmaz (Meta AI Research, FAIR). Preprint; the only venue marking on the PDF is "arXiv:2308.04592v1 [cs.CL] 8 Aug 2023".

COVERAGE: 19 of 19 pages, 76,921 of 76,921 chars. Body, limitations, Tables 1-14, Appendices A-B read in full; references (p10-12) skimmed. Figures 6, 7 and 9 are graphics, so only their captions were extracted, not the plotted values.

CLAIMS

- claim: A 7B fine-tuned critic beats Alpaca-7B and narrowly beats SelFee-7B and ChatGPT when GPT-4 is the pairwise judge.
  number: average win rate 87.0 / 53.0 / 56.0
  setup: Shepherd is LLaMA-7B fine-tuned on about 8K examples. 352 instances: 50 from each of 6 public sets plus 52 CritiqueEval. Judge is GPT-4-0613 with the Figure 5 prompt (A/B/"Neither is significantly better").
  quote: "Shepherd vs. Alpaca 78.0 90.0 82.0 87.0 91.0 90.0 92.3 87.0 / Shepherd vs. SelFee 52.0 55.0 58.0 51.0 46.0 57.0 51.9 53.0 / Shepherd vs. ChatGPT 55.0 65.0 47.0 47.0 66.0 48.0 61.5 56.0"
  where: Table 3, p8

- claim: Under human pairwise judgement Shepherd still beats Alpaca and SelFee but only ties ChatGPT.
  number: 72.4 / 59.7 / 49.6
  setup: same 352 instances; number of raters and agreement not reported.
  quote: "Shepherd vs. ChatGPT 38.0 59.0 39.0 49.0 43.0 52.0 66.3 49.6"
  where: Table 4, p8

- claim: GPT-4 as an independent 1-7 Likert rater inflates scores and contradicts humans.
  number: Alpaca 4.7 (GPT-4) vs 2.91 (human)
  setup: Figure 4 rubric, where 1-3 means wrong judgement and 4-7 correct. GPT-4 rates each critique alone; humans saw all four models' critiques together.
  quote: "Alpaca obtains an average score of 4.7, meaning most feedback have a correct judgment of the response, while human gives an average score of 2.91"
  where: section 5.3, p7; Tables 5-6, p9

- claim: The GPT-4 Likert ranking differs from the human one: GPT-4 puts ChatGPT 6.25, SelFee 5.49, Shepherd 5.37, Alpaca 4.69; humans put SelFee at 3.84, well below Shepherd at 4.41.
  number: as stated
  setup: same as above; authors attribute it to GPT-4 rewarding generic suggestions.
  quote: "The likert score assigned by GPT-4 appears to be favoring a specific format."
  where: p7; Tables 5-6, p9

- claim: The authors recommend pairwise over Likert for an LLM judge.
  number: none
  quote: "we recommend using GPT-4 to rate in a pairwise comparison style, which aligns well with human evaluation."
  where: p8

- claim: Shepherd gives more top-rated critiques than ChatGPT but also more wrong verdicts.
  number: none (plot values not extractable)
  quote: "more feedback with score 7) although it tends to generate feedback with wrong judgements (more feedback with score 2)"
  where: section 5.2, p7

- claim: Training data is small and curated; the comparator SelFee used far more.
  number: 8K vs 178K; 1,317 human-annotated examples at $8 each
  setup: community data from Stack Exchange and 16 subreddits, filtered by keywords, edit history and vote scores; one expert annotator per example (RWS Moravia).
  quote: "SelFee was finetuned on a dataset of 178K examples (some of which overlapped with our evaluation data) whereasShepherd was only finetuned on a dataset of 8K"; "We end up with 1,317 high quality examples in total"; "Each example is quoted for $8"
  where: p7; p4

- claim: A contamination-controlled test set was built from recent Reddit posts.
  number: 52 questions, June 2022 to June 2023
  quote: "CritiqueEval, containing 52 Pushshift questions posted from June 2022 to June 2023"
  where: p5

- claim: GPT-4 misjudged a critique even with the ground truth supplied, and penalised the one critic that caught an error it could not see itself.
  number: GPT-4 score 5 for an incorrect critique; SelFee 6, ChatGPT 4, Shepherd 2
  quote: "GPT-4 gives SelFee score 6, ChatGPT score 4, Shepherd score 2. However, only Shepherd successfully points out the error in the answer."
  where: Tables 13-14, p19

LIMITS
- Conceded: more annotators and tasks are needed; GPT-4 evaluation "can be unstable and inaccurate"; human evaluation is hard where domain knowledge is required (Table 2).
- Not shown: no inter-annotator agreement, rater count, confidence intervals or significance tests, despite "significantly"; no correlation statistic between GPT-4 and human judgements; no position-swap control in the pairwise prompt; no cost or latency figures; no test of whether critiques improve downstream outputs; no model release is stated (the footnote releases data only).
- Sample is small (50 per dataset), and the "ties with ChatGPT" result flips by dataset (38.0 on AlpacaFarm, 66.3 on CritiqueEval).
- Checkpoint selection used the same GPT-4 protocol later used for evaluation, on a 20-example held-out set.
- SelFee's training data overlaps the test set (33 of 50 AlpacaFarm instances), which favours SelFee.
- Dated: baselines are GPT-3.5 Turbo, Alpaca-7B, SelFee-7B; the judge is GPT-4-0613.

BUILDS ON: LLaMA (Touvron et al., 2023) as base; SelFee (Ye et al., 2023); Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023); Saunders et al. (2022) self-critiquing models; Self-Correct (Welleck et al., 2023); Critic (Gou et al., 2023); GPT-4-as-evaluator from Liu et al. (2023, G-Eval), Wang et al. (2023c), Zhou et al. (2023, LIMA); evaluator bias from Wang et al. (2023a) and Aiyappa et al. (2023).

CODE: no code. Pairwise judge prompt (Figure 5, p6), verbatim: "Two pieces of feedback have been provided for the same response to a particular question. Which one can point out key errors contained in the answer or provide constructive suggestions? ... A: Feedback 1 is significantly better. B: Feedback 2 is significantly better. C: Neither is significantly better." The 7-point Likert rubric is Figure 4, p5.

FIGURES: Figure 2, p3, "Preference evaluation using GPT-4 as the evaluator, comparing Shepherd with 3 different competing models across 7 different datasets." It sits beside Figure 3 (the human version), so one glance shows the GPT-4 judge and humans agreeing on Alpaca and SelFee but diverging on ChatGPT.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions aimed at the reader; the only instruction text is the paper's own judge and annotator prompts.
- Internal inconsistencies in the source, all checked by my own arithmetic on the printed rows:
  - Table 5's Avg column does not match the row means. Shepherd's row averages about 4.55 (printed 4.41) and ChatGPT's about 4.31 (printed 4.59), so the printed "ChatGPT slightly ahead on human Likert" reverses on the per-dataset numbers.
  - Table 4's Alpaca average is printed 72.4; the row mean is about 75.1.
  - Figures 2-3 print different numbers from Tables 3-4 (e.g. 81.0% wins vs 87.0 win rate). The tables appear to count a tie as half a win, but the paper never defines "win rate".
  - Section 4.1 lists "CommonsenseQA"; the tables say "CosmosQA".
  - Raters are called both "crowd worker" and "expert annotators".
- Figure 2-3 legends extracted as garbled glyphs, so which of the two smaller percentages is "tie" versus "loss" is not certain from the text.
